nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Strong year-round sun powers the rainforest canopy and the algae and plankton of the reef.

nodes.name: Heavy rainfall
nodes.desc: The islands are wet. Rain feeds the rainforest and runs down steep slopes to the sea.

nodes.name: Cool, clear reef water
nodes.desc: Corals live close to their heat limit. During marine heatwaves they bleach and can die, while reef algae spread.

nodes.name: Volcanic soil
nodes.desc: Weathered volcanic rock and rotting leaf litter feed the forest trees.

nodes.name: Breadfruit
nodes.desc: A large fruiting tree of villages and forest edges. Its fruit is eaten by flying foxes and rats.

nodes.name: Coconut palm
nodes.desc: A coastal palm found around the shores of the islands. Flying foxes and rats eat its fruit.

nodes.name: Screw pine
nodes.desc: A coastal tree with fruit that flying foxes feed on.

nodes.name: Reef algae
nodes.desc: Algae growing on reef rock feed turtles, parrotfish and surgeonfish. They spread when corals die.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Drifting algae in the ocean water that feed zooplankton at the base of the open-water food chain.

nodes.name: Samoa flying fox
nodes.desc: A fruit bat that feeds on fruit, leaves and flowers in forest. Hunting and forest clearance threaten it.

nodes.name: Pacific flying fox
nodes.desc: A fruit bat that eats fruit, pollen and nectar, and pollinates some trees as it feeds.

nodes.name: Polynesian rat
nodes.desc: An omnivore spread across the Pacific by settlers. It eats seeds, fruit, insects, lizards and bird eggs.

nodes.name: Green sea turtle
nodes.desc: Adults graze on algae and seagrass in shallow water. Tiger sharks are their main predator.

nodes.name: Parrotfish
nodes.desc: Reef fish that scrape algae from rock and coral. Grazing keeps algae from smothering the reef.

nodes.name: Surgeonfish
nodes.desc: Schooling fish that graze algae around coral reefs.

nodes.name: Reef-building corals
nodes.desc: Branching corals build the reef structure. They catch plankton and shelter many fish.

nodes.name: Zooplankton
nodes.desc: Tiny animals of the plankton that graze phytoplankton and feed corals and fish.

nodes.name: Feral cat
nodes.desc: An introduced predator. Cats hunt rats and small animals that lack defenses against ambush hunters.

nodes.name: Ghost crab
nodes.desc: A burrowing beach crab that scavenges carrion and takes turtle hatchlings.

nodes.name: Crown-of-thorns starfish
nodes.desc: A starfish that eats hard coral polyps. Outbreaks can strip large areas of living coral.

nodes.name: Blacktip reef shark
nodes.desc: A shallow reef shark that eats small bony fish, squid and crabs.

nodes.name: Tiger shark
nodes.desc: A large shark that eats sea turtles, fish and smaller sharks, and also scavenges dead animals.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi, bacteria and invertebrates that break down leaf litter and dead animals and return nutrients to the soil.
